$description: The Inspector's **Logic** tab — everything about how the selected element BEHAVES, as a Jx document over the kit. Plan §6.5 re-split the inspector by task rather than by data type: wiring a `$switch`, wiring a repeater to a collection and wiring a click handler are one job, and they were three, split across two tabs because a `$switch` is stored as a property and a click handler as a property-shaped function. So there are four sections here — Repeating list, Condition, Events, and a custom element's outward contract (Observed Attributes · CSS Properties · CSS Parts) — and each of them is a projection. The adapter (`panels/events-panel.ts`) keeps every decision: what the selection is, which rungs a position permits, what a handler currently holds, which elements of a multi-selection disagree about a key, and what a commit writes. Nothing here reads the document, asks the schema a question or knows what a Value Source is. Two islands, both through `onNodeCreated` (studio-ui-guidelines.md §9.4): `[part="control-host"]` receives the expression editor, which is a lit surface of its own, and `[part="statements-host"]` receives the `statements` surface, which is a mounted document of its own. Every bindable row carries `data-prop`, which is what `inspector/field:<prop>` addresses.

style.$description: The tab's own layout, and nothing else. `.style-sidebar` and `.style-section-body` are NOT transcribed: the first was a scroll container the dock already provides, and the second existed to put padding inside a Spectrum accordion item, which `jx-accordion-item` does itself. What is left is the two vocabularies this tab has that no other surface does — a declared event, and an event binding — plus the one empty state a document cannot borrow from `panels/empty-state.ts`.

& [part=\"empty\"].$description: The one empty-state pattern (§11.2), drawn here because a document cannot render a lit helper. It is a copy rather than a move — every panel still lit renders through that helper — and it goes when the last of them converts.

& [part=\"field\"] > [part=\"label\"]:em.$description: A row whose control names itself — an expression editor draws its own Operator / Target / Value rows — has no second label to draw. `jx-field` takes the empty label out of the accessible name by leaving it empty; this takes it out of the layout.

& [part=\"binding\"].$description: One `on*` key and whatever produces it. A box, for the reason a statement card is one: a handler CONTAINS a body, and the border is what says where one binding stops and the next begins.

children.$description: Repeating list. Filter and Sort are always drawn: they used to hide behind `+ Add filter`, which seeded `{ $ref: "#/state/" }` — a binding to the empty pointer, which is not a signal — so the row opened already bound to nothing and the only way to type a literal was to cycle the mode ring twice (§11.4). A repeater has exactly three inputs, and an empty row states that better than a button does.

map.$description: A bindable value as a first-class field row. Every position it serves is a single-line expression — a collection, a filter, a sort key, a `$switch` — so it draws one widget rather than dispatching over a widget type: the textarea and checkbox arms the lit version carried had no caller in either tab. The set dot clears the position outright and is disabled where the position is mandatory; the source chip opens the rung picker rather than cycling, so any rung the position permits is one action away (§6.3).

children.$description: Condition. A `$switch` discriminant is a `$ref` and nothing else, so From data… is its only rung — de-escalating it would delete the key and demote the node — and the adapter says so by locking the row's source chip rather than by this document knowing what a `SwitchDef` is.

map.$description: A bindable value as a first-class field row. Every position it serves is a single-line expression — a collection, a filter, a sort key, a `$switch` — so it draws one widget rather than dispatching over a widget type: the textarea and checkbox arms the lit version carried had no caller in either tab. The set dot clears the position outright and is disabled where the position is mandatory; the source chip opens the rung picker rather than cycling, so any rung the position permits is one action away (§6.3).

children.$description: Events. A repeater is not an element — it has no `on*` position to bind, and offering Add Event on one writes a handler onto a node the renderer never mounts — so the adapter withholds the whole section rather than this document asking what a repeater is.

map.$description: One `on*` key. The Mixed contract (§6.5) splits in two and this row shows both halves: which events exist, how each is produced, and its removal are properties of the BATCH — binding one handler to six buttons is a single decision, so those three controls write to every selected element in one transaction — while what a handler CONTAINS is the PRIMARY's, because six elements do not share one body and broadcasting a keystroke into six of them would destroy five. The dot says `mixed` when the selected elements disagree; the body below it stays the primary's.

children.$description: The event NAME, and it is free-form rather than a list of ten. The menu offers what this element already binds plus the ten worth suggesting, and its last row asks for any other name through the one prompt dialog Studio has — so `ondragover`, `onpointerdown` and every custom event a component emits are bindable, which is exactly what §6.5 asks for and what the closed picker refused.

The same ladder every other bindable position in Studio offers, in the same four words. It used to read Inline code / Expression / Existing function — a fourth private dialect for the one ladder §6.6 collapses, so a user who learned "Formula" on a property row met "Expression" here and had no reason to think they were the same thing.

Statements or Code, for an inline function only. A structured body is a `JxStatement[]` and a code body is a string, so the toggle is a change of REPRESENTATION rather than of view — which is why it is drawn beside the body it rewrites rather than in the source ladder above it.

statements.$description: An island: `surfaces/statements.ts` mounts its own document in here, named by the handler it edits (`inspector/statements:<key>`), because a node with two structured handlers stamped one id on two elements and `resolveRegion` took the second.

children.$description: The custom element's outward contract: what a page may set from markup, what it may override, and what it may reach into. Three read-only lists — this is a report, not a form — drawn only on a component's root.

children.textContent: Attributes let a page set this component from markup. Name an "attribute" on a data entry to expose it here.

map.$description: A read-only name and what it maps to. The Content tab had three near-identical hand-written flex rows for these; they are one shape now, and this is it.
